problem: The answer describes the t statistic as a ratio of independent standard normal and chi-square variables. That is not the definition: the t statistic is Z divided by the square root of an independent chi-square variable divided by its degrees of freedom. The square root and division by df are missing, so the explanation is technically wrong.
fix: Say: t = (x̄ − μ)/(S/√n) = Z / √(χ²ₙ₋₁/(n−1)), where Z ~ N(0,1) and χ²ₙ₋₁ are independent; then t has n−1 df and gives t tests and t intervals.
